_comment: nightmare config-a ("shipping firmware"): which components the build used.
zlib 1.2.11      10 sources compiled under its root          -> used
sqlite3 3.41.2   prebuilt .a passed to the linker            -> used (link input)
cjson-prebuilt   prebuilt .a passed to the linker            -> used (link input)
uthash           header-only, named only as an -I path       -> used (weaker rung)
freertos         in the tree, not compiled in this config    -> UNUSED
stb              in the tree, compiled in NO config          -> UNUSED
conan zlib 1.3.1 declared only: no location in the repo      -> not judged, kept
Hand-authored, deliberately not machine-blessed (see fixtures/trim/). The
trace is the REAL `bomwerk observe` trace of bomwerk/nightmare, minimized:
CMake's compiler probes and the ld --help/-v/LTO runs (non-deterministic
/tmp paths) were dropped, absolute paths became @FIXTURE_ROOT@/tree and the
shim path became the plain tool name. The tree is IDENTICAL for config-a and
config-b; only the trace differs. That is the corpus's central claim.
The ar record is never evidence by itself; the final cc record has no -c, so
it is link-mode and does not count as a compile.
The two prebuilt archives (sqlite-prebuilt, cjson-prebuilt) are judged from the
link line: config-a passes each .a to the linker by absolute path, so each root
gets one link input. Their include directories are on the -I path as well, but
a link input outranks a header-only mention. The tree holds only their headers
and an empty lib/ (a .gitkeep): trim canonicalizes a link input's DIRECTORY, not
the file, so the directory must exist and the archive itself need not.
